justification: The evidence supports some operational robustness beyond nominal conditions: performance remains high under multiple predefined perturbations, formatting variation, OCR degradation, random removal of non-critical fields, and the system flags most out-of-distribution documents. However, the available evidence does not fully establish robustness for the described deployment context because robustness is not demonstrated across the full operational scope, and the out-of-distribution mechanism missed 73 of 1,200 excluded-class documents. The results therefore justify a qualified, partial attribution rather than a full attribution of operational robustness.
evidence_used: With 10% randomly removed non-critical fields, accuracy was 93.7%.
With the predefined OCR degradation transformation, accuracy was 92.1%.
Across the predefined formatting-variation set, accuracy ranged from 91.6% to 94.8%.
An out-of-distribution test set contained 1,200 documents from document classes excluded from training.
Of the 1,200 out-of-distribution samples, 1,127 were flagged by the out-of-distribution mechanism.
The validation protocol contains three predefined perturbation tests; corresponding accuracies were 92.8%, 90.9%, and 93.4%.
A separate validation team reproduced the reported tests.
limitations: Evidence is limited to the predefined validation and perturbation set; it does not cover the full deployment scope described.
The available information does not specify operational thresholds for acceptable robustness in this context.
Out-of-distribution detection is incomplete, since 73 of 1,200 excluded-class documents were not flagged.
Nominal validation accuracy alone would not be sufficient, so the conclusion depends on the limited set of perturbation and distribution-shift tests provided.
